html:
The Haush, who called themselves Mánekenk, were a hunting people of the far eastern tip of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, on the Mitre Peninsula in what is now Argentina.

They hunted guanaco and seals and gathered shellfish along the shore. Their language was related to that of the Selk'nam, who pressed them into the far corner of the island. Sheep ranches, gold seekers and disease in the late 1800s destroyed them, and by the early 1900s they had died out as a people. The canoe living Yagán lived across the channels to the south.
sum: The Haush, who called themselves Mánekenk, were a hunting people of the far eastern tip of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, on the Mitre Peninsula in what is now Argentina.
